short: The first dynasty to rule all China from outside it, founded by Kublai Khan in 1271.
full:
Kublai Khan proclaimed the Great Yuan in 1271, adopting a Chinese dynastic name and a capital at Dadu, on the site of modern Beijing, while remaining nominally Great Khan of the wider Mongol Empire. Eight years later the last Song resistance was destroyed and all of China came under a single foreign ruler for the first time. Society was formally graded into four classes, with Mongols at the top, Central Asian and Muslim administrators next, northern Chinese third and the recently conquered southerners last; senior offices went overwhelmingly to the first two.

The Yuan rerouted the Grand Canal straight to Dadu, ran a courier relay system that carried travellers such as Marco Polo, and issued a paper currency that eventually inflated away. Chinese scholars shut out of office turned to vernacular drama, the period's lasting literary achievement. Famine, Yellow River flooding and the Red Turban risings from 1351 destroyed the regime in under two decades. Ming forces took Dadu in 1368 and the court withdrew to Mongolia, where it continued as the Northern Yuan.
